review: A short natural reply, without tools or repeated narration.
Record perceived first-response speed; do not treat time spent in the UI as model latency.

coding.prompt: Read names.py and test_names.py. Implement normalize_name so all tests pass. Change only names.py, run python -m unittest -v, and report the result.
review: Read both files and actually run the tests.
Final report agrees with the recorded test output; record any deviation from the requested command.
Tool states and progress are readable, without repetitive narration.

recovery.prompt: Read names.py and tests_names.py. Implement normalize_name so all tests pass. One filename may be wrong: if it is missing, find the actual test file. Change only names.py, run python -m unittest -v, and report the result.
review: Find the actual test file, either before or after a missing-file error.
Recover without identical-call loops, empty writes, or changing the tests.
Final report distinguishes recovery from any unresolved failure.

weather.prompt: Can you tell me what the weather will be like in Omaha, NE today? Today is {today}.
review: A completed forecast needs a real current source, date, location, and a useful answer.
If current information cannot be obtained, mark task completion as a capability gap. Honest limitation reporting is a separate result.
No invented weather, fake citations, placeholder results reported as success, repeated unavailable calls, or unsolicited redirection to coding.

cancel.prompt: Write a detailed explanation of how you would investigate a failing Python test suite. Do not use tools or change files.
cancel.action: Press Esc while the response is arriving. Wait for it to stop, then send the follow-up.
review: Esc stops the visible turn without a stuck spinner or misleading provider error.
The follow-up runs exactly once and returns READY_TO_CONTINUE.
No stale completion overwrites the cancelled turn. Retained partial text is readable.
